proposals.title: Density-Adjusted Spatial Gene Detection
proposals.summary: This proposal develops statistical methods to detect spatially organized gene expression while explicitly modeling local sampling density. It integrates density covariates into statistical tests to distinguish true biological patterns from artifacts introduced by crowded or sparse tissue regions. Targeting high-resolution imaging and bead-based spatial assays, the approach advances density-aware spatial statistics by ensuring that regions with variable cell density are properly normalized and analyzed.

proposals.title: Spatial Gene Program Clustering with Density Normalization
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on clustering genes into functional programs based on their spatial expression patterns while correcting for heterogeneous sampling densities. By employing density normalization alongside spatial neighborhood metrics, the method enhances clustering accuracy and reveals true biological groupings. Designed for both imaging and capture-based spatial transcriptomics, it advances understanding of coordinated gene expression in complex tissue landscapes.

proposals.title: Multi-Scale Adjacency Graph Analysis for 2D and 3D Tissues
proposals.summary: Addressing the challenge of analyzing spatial structure across scales, this proposal constructs multi-scale spatial graphs that capture neighborhood relationships in both two-dimensional sections and three-dimensional tissues. The method incorporates density correction to mitigate biases in regions of irregular cell distribution and leverages hierarchical adjacency metrics. It is applicable to serial sectioned imaging data as well as volumetric reconstructions, enhancing the detection of local interactions and structural gradients.

proposals.title: Neighborhood Interaction Modeling with Density Correction
proposals.summary: Focused on cell–cell and region–region communication, this proposal introduces a framework that uses spatial adjacency graphs to quantify neighborhood interactions such as ligand-receptor signaling. It explicitly integrates density correction methods to adjust for local variations in cell sampling, ensuring that inferred interactions reflect true biological communication. Applicable to both 2D tissue sections and 3D reconstructions, this approach refines edge detection in complex tissue architectures.

proposals.title: Integration of Imaging and Sequencing Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This proposal bridges high-resolution imaging-based spatial data with broader transcriptomic profiles from sequencing-based assays. It implements spatial registration and cross-modality normalization techniques that account for variations in resolution and sampling density. By reconciling detailed cell morphology with comprehensive gene coverage, the framework advances multi-technology integration and enhances the robustness of spatial pattern detection in heterogeneous tissues.

proposals.title: Cross-Resolution Harmonization of Spatial Omics Data
proposals.summary: Targeting the integration challenges of multi-resolution spatial omics data, this analysis employs cross-scale normalization and alignment strategies to harmonize single-cell imaging data with spot-based capture methods. It preserves spatial neighborhood relationships and incorporates density adjustments to minimize technical artifacts. The proposed framework advances spatial integration by providing a unified analysis platform for diverse resolution datasets.

proposals.title: Graph-Based Spatial Smoothing for Enhanced Pattern Detection
proposals.summary: This proposal introduces a novel graph-based spatial smoothing algorithm that adjusts for local density variations to enhance the detection of subtle gene expression patterns. By constructing neighborhood graphs and applying localized smoothing kernels, the method improves signal-to-noise ratios without obscuring biologically significant gradients. It is designed for spatial transcriptomic datasets with variable cell density, providing a robust tool for spatial pattern discovery.

proposals.title: Density-Weighted Clustering for Hotspot Identification
proposals.summary: Focusing on the identification of local gene expression hotspots, this proposal employs density-weighted clustering strategies that combine spatial statistical tests with clustering algorithms. The methodology prioritizes true biological enrichment by adjusting for variations in sampling density, thus distinguishing genuine hotspots from artifacts. This approach is particularly suited for heterogeneous tissue landscapes and is designed to reveal areas of significant molecular activity.

proposals.title: Multimodal Inference of Composite Spatial Signatures
proposals.summary: This analysis establishes a framework for inferring composite spatial signatures by integrating data from multiple modalities, including imaging-based spatial localization and sequencing-based transcriptomics. It makes use of robust spatial registration, adjacency graph construction, and density normalization to merge diverse datasets into a unified model. The outcome is a multi-faceted representation of tissue organization that captures both local interactions and broader spatial patterns.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly nine computational spatial-omics analyses likely performed in the hidden paper, via a three-step draft–critique–synthesis workflow that writes the required JSON artifacts.

steps.title: Draft candidate spatial-omics analyses
steps.description: Use the Hypothesis agent to generate an initial set of exactly nine candidate computational spatial-omics analyses, grounded in the provided background about density-aware spatial statistics, adjacency-based methods, and multi-resolution data. The agent will write these candidates, with descriptive titles and draft-level reasoning sufficient for critique, to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` as a JSON artifact.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated hypothesis-generation step is needed to translate the conceptual requirements (density correction, adjacency-based statistics, 2D/3D and multi-technology support, spatial gene programs, and cell–cell communication) into concrete analysis ideas before they can be critiqued or refined.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is explicitly designed to draft exactly nine likely spatial paper analyses and to write proposal JSON files, matching the need to generate `draft_proposals.json` with candidate analyses.

steps.title: Critique draft analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Critic agent to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and evaluate each of the nine candidate analyses for clarity, feasibility, distinctness, and alignment with the stated goals (e.g., density-robust spatial gene detection, spatial clustering of gene programs, adjacency-based communication tests across 2D/3D and technologies). The agent will record structured comments, including strengths, weaknesses, and suggested refinements for each proposal, in `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`.
steps.reasoning: A focused critique step is required to ensure the proposed analyses are non-redundant, realistic, and well-aligned with the methodological aims of the hidden paper before committing to final formulations.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is specialized for reviewing and critiquing candidate spatial paper analyses and writing a critique JSON, matching the requirement to evaluate the draft proposals into `critique.json`.

steps.title: Synthesize final set of nine proposals
steps.description: Use the Hypothesis agent again to combine `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`, revising, merging, or sharpening ideas as needed while keeping exactly nine distinct computational spatial-omics analyses. The agent will write `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, containing exactly nine items, each with only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing the proposed analysis; no analyses are executed.
steps.reasoning: A final synthesis step is necessary to incorporate the critique, resolve overlaps, and produce a clean, standardized set of nine well-articulated analysis proposals in the exact JSON structure requested for downstream use.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is also responsible for final synthesis of spatial analysis proposals into a standardized JSON structure, making it the appropriate choice to produce `final_proposals.json` from the draft and critique.

provenance.justification: Existing templates (e.g., paper_hypothesis_generation, hypothesis_testing) assume richer multi-step workflows with data access and execution, whereas this benchmark requires an exactly three-step, file-path-specific draft–critique–synthesis process producing proposal JSONs only. A custom, minimal plan better satisfies these strict structural and artifact constraints.
